A vignette to demonstrate how to use PsyR to manually calculate Roy's Greatest Characteristic Root (GCR), as described in @roy1957some. This is useful for...

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(PsyR)
library(tidyverse)
```

## Roy's GCR

To generate Roy's GCR, we first need to fit some data to a MANOVA model. We will demonstrate this using the `social_anxiety` dataframe, which contains the results of a 3 x (4) between x within experiment that assessed a new treatment for social anxiety. Here, *N* = 90 participants were randomly allocated to one of three levels of the between-subjects independent variable: a minimum contact control condition, a standard treatment, or a new treatment. All participants were then measured on four occasions: immediately before treatment, immediately after treatment, at a 3 month follow-up, and at a 6 month follow-up. The dependent variable is social anxiety rating, where a lower score is indicative of lower social anxiety.

Let's load the data, then call the `head()` function to print the first 5 rows.

```{r load}
data(social_anxiety)
head(social_anxiety, 5)
```

Let's also tidy the data, pivoting it to wide-form.

```{r, wideform}

social_anxiety  <- social_anxiety %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Session, 
    values_from = Score
  )

```

Now we run a MANOVA analysis to get Roy's GCR of the co-variance matrix.

```{r, multimod}

fit <- manova(cbind(Pre, Post, FU1, FU2) ~ Group, data = social_anxiety)
summary(fit, test = "Roy")

```

So we are working with a value of 0.3903

## compute probability

Now we compute the probability of observing a GCR of 0.39 of our analysis.

```{r, set params}

theta = 0.3903
v_w = 3 # df within = number of levels of the within subject factor - 1
v_b = 2 # df between = number of levels of the between subject factor - 1
v_e = 87 # df error = total number of subjects - number of groups


```

Now the parameters are set, we can observe the probability of theta given v_w, v_b, and v_e

```{r, compute prob}

p = pgcr(theta, v_w, v_b, v_e)
p
```
